findings.evidence: PDF p.148 (printed p.124), figure text: "SLO 2 s (TTFT budget)". Caption on the same page: "...while 1% of requests exceed the 2 s request-latency line — the p95 TTFT ceiling (Ch 4, Table 4-1 Latency row; Canonical Workload box), not the 1.2 s design budget — a superset of TTFT violations...". Ch 4 (PDF p.110, printed p.86) states the opposite terminology: "The two thresholds are not interchangeable: 1.2 s is the design budget, ≤ 2 s is the p95 ceiling the budget relaxes to, and any pass/fail judgement on a measured distribution is made against the p95 ceiling, not the budget."
findings.issue: The in-figure axis label calls the 2-second line the "TTFT budget", contradicting both the figure's own caption and the book's load-bearing SLO terminology (1.2 s = TTFT design budget; ≤2 s = p95 ceiling). A reader reading the figure alone will take the SLO as a 2 s budget rather than a p95 ceiling that relaxes a 1.2 s budget, and the label is doubly wrong because the line is drawn on the request-latency axis while named for TTFT (request latency ≥ TTFT, which the caption itself notes flags a superset of violations).
findings.fix_instruction: Change the in-figure label from "SLO 2 s (TTFT budget)" to "p95 TTFT ceiling 2 s" (or "SLO 2 s (p95 TTFT ceiling)"), so the figure label matches the caption's terminology and the Ch 4 definition; add a note that the line is drawn on request latency, not TTFT.

findings.evidence: In-figure annotation on the rendered Fig 6.2 (PDF p.148, printed p.124) reads verbatim: "SLO 2 s (TTFT budget)". The caption on the same page correctly states the line is "the p95 TTFT ceiling (Ch 4, Table 4-1 Latency row; Canonical Workload box), not the 1.2 s design budget". Ch. 4 (PDF p.110) fixes the terminology: "The two thresholds are not interchangeable: 1.2 s is the design budget, ≤ 2 s is the p95 ceiling the budget relaxes to", and Ch. 6 §6.3.1 (PDF p.147) repeats: "a ceiling above the 1.2 s design budget, not a second budget".
findings.issue: The figure's internal annotation attaches the word "budget" to the 2 s line, directly contradicting the book's own load-bearing budget-vs-ceiling distinction that the surrounding text and the figure's own caption enforce (1.2 s = design budget; 2 s = p95 ceiling). A reader quoting the figure would misstate the SLO basis.
findings.fix_instruction: Change the in-plot annotation from "SLO 2 s (TTFT budget)" to "SLO 2 s (p95 TTFT ceiling)" (or "p95 ceiling ≤ 2 s"), keeping the caption unchanged. Then sweep all other figures/tables that plot the 2 s line (e.g., any Ch. 14/15 SLO plots) for the same mislabel.
